text:
maria: quick sync — I'm running a head-to-head of two harness configs for emb/rerank perf. trying to get an apples-to-apples baseline across: batching heuristics (grouped vs striped), vector dims (128/256/512), payload sizes (ids only vs ids+meta ~1kB), and kv cache states (cold/warm).
aj: nice. what infra are you using? dedicated or hosted?
maria: dedicated-pprod GPU pool (A100-ish). using same model binary and same kernel set for both runs so kernel selection is isolated.
sophie: can you paste the exact invocations? want to replicate on my lane.
maria: sure — run used:
```
./harness \\--model rerank-v1.bin \\--workload replay \\--batching grouped \\--vectors 256 \\--payload-mode ids+meta \\--kv-policy prefix_cache=true,warmup=1000 \\--out artifacts/rep-grouped.json
```
and synthetic config:
```
./harness \\--model rerank-v1.bin \\--workload synthetic_smasher \\--batching striped \\--vectors 256 \\--payload-mode ids_only \\--kv-policy prefix_cache=false,warmup=0 \\--seed 42 \\--out artifacts/synth-striped.json
```
aj: thanks. two quick flags: make sure `--kernel-override` is unset so runtime picks kernels automatically, and run with `--trace=cpu` for a subset to profile kernel hot paths.
perfbot: automated summary (rep-grouped vs synth-striped, vectors=256): p50/p95/p99 tokens-per-ms: 0.85/0.52/0.25 vs 0.82/0.47/0.18. tail worse when payload includes meta. kv warm reduced p99 by ~35%. attached perf-ids: s3://redwood-artifacts/1845001234/summary.csv
devin: interesting that grouped batching increased p95 but improved p50 — might be due to batch formation latency under striped traffic. we should capture batch size distribution during runs (histogram).
sophie: i'll run the 128/512 sweeps later today. any preference for payload permutations?
maria: please run both ids_only and ids+smallmeta (~256B) for each dim. keep `--model` identical and seed deterministic for synthetic. also set `--kv-policy prefix_cache=true,warmup=200` and a cold run with `warmup=0`.
aj: note: when comparing dims, also check memory working set and nvlink traffic — larger dims push kernel selection to different GEMM paths.
perfbot: quick note: kernel-selection toggles tested: autotune=on vs off. autotune on picked int8 kernels for 256/512 in 80% of cases. int8 reduced median latency by 12% but increased p99 by 9% on ids+meta cases.
maria: next steps: 1) sophie does dim+payload matrix runs 2) aj captures traces for 10% of requests 3) devin prepares batch-size histograms + kv-hit traces 4) i'll assemble an internal notebook comparing p50/p95/p99 and batch-size CDFs, plus kernel-choice breakdown.
sophie: on it. will post artifacts in `#eng-platform-artifacts` and link here. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — if anyone sees any perf regressions in the artifacts (unexpected p99 spikes), flag them here and we'll bisect with kernel toggles.
aj: one more thought — add a short synthetic with heavier seq length tail to stress KV cache eviction.
maria: good call. adding `--seq-tail=heavy` to the synthetic plan.
perfbot: enqueued follow-up job: sweep dims {128,256,512} x payloads {ids,ids+256B,ids+1kB} x kv {cold,warm} — estimated runtime 6h. will post run ids when done.
devin: perfect. once sweeps finish i'll run a quick A/B: quantized vs fp16 kernels for the p99 offenders.
sophie: will upload raw batch traces. linking artifacts when ready: https://s3.redwoodlabs/internal/1845001234/
maria: wrapping up — thanks everyone. i'll open a short RFC with the benchmark harness config and recommended reproducibility checklist (model hash, kernel flags, seed, infra snapshot).
